body:
which system? backtrace should be easy to get, see [wiki](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#debugging).

Thanks for bisecting!

cc @mhinz

```
sudo apt install systemd-coredump
2>&1 coredumpctl -1 gdb | tee -a bt.txt
thread apply all bt full
```

Post the `bt.txt` file here.
Do I run nvim, then that command? Nvim doesn't give a core dump, it just immediately closes.

> Do I run nvim, then that command? 

Provoke the crash using `nvim`, then run that command. Your OS keeps a global list of coredumps.



> Nvim doesn't give a core dump

What leads you to believe that? With newer systems there is no `core` file. Hence the instructions I gave above.

on macOS you can just do this:

    open -a Console

Read https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#debugging if you still have questions.
When I run nvim and then the command above, I get: `no match found`.

`ERROR 2019-02-09T16:42:03.813 17277 xmalloc:105: XXX`

That's the whole file when I run `NVIM_LOG_FILE=file nvim`

Thanks, that confirms OOM. 

Roughly how much free RAM is on your system before running Nvim?

Here's the output of `free -h`:
```
              total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available
Mem:            31G        1.0G         24G        6.7M        5.5G         29G
Swap:           33G          0B         33G
```

issue.title: terminal: Fix potential invalid local 'scrollback'

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
TermOpen autocmd may set local 'scrollback' to -1, this needs to be
adjusted as in on_scrollback_option_changed().

fixes #9588 (OOM, out of memory)
